seed.legacy-vs-engineered-laptop-encryption.m:
# Legacy-vs-Engineered Analysis: Laptop Encryption

## Control as a claim
Claim: Every employee laptop has full-disk encryption enabled.
Truth lives today in: the MDM device API (per-device encryption status), reachable right now.

## Five-problem scorecard (legacy)
- Manual toil, trivial output: an analyst collects a handful of encryption screenshots each quarter.
- Transactional relationship: IT is chased for evidence near audit time, treated as an evidence source.
- Whack-a-mole: a single drifted laptop is fixed once it is noticed, not the enrollment gap that caused it.
- Closed-framework focus: effort optimizes the SOC 2 binder wording rather than actual fleet encryption.
- Commoditized compliance: prior "automation" just emailed one screenshot faster, adding no assurance.

## Legacy arrow
Verified today as framework -> controls -> implementation -> evidence -> audit: reality is consulted
LAST, by hand, once a quarter, on a small sample.

## Engineered arrow (seven-stage loop)
- UNDERSTAND: the claim is "every laptop is encrypted, right now."
- LOCATE: the truth lives in the MDM device API.
- QUERY: authenticated, fully paginated call listing every enrolled device.
- EVALUATE: encryption flag == on for every device, expressed as policy-as-code.
- EVIDENCE: the full API response plus the pass/fail verdict, written to a versioned store.
- MONITOR: re-run on a schedule; alert the owner when any device flips to non-compliant.
- OWN: a named owner, with time-to-remediate-drift as the product metric.

## Inversion statement
Reality -> policy: instead of asking the binder whether the fleet complied, we ask the fleet
continuously and let what it reports drive the policy and the proof.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gate.sh — the CORE LOGIC of the §6 lab, isolated for testing.
#
# Reads a Checkov-shaped JSON scan result and a control map, applies a severity
# floor, maps every failed check to the control it enforces, decides PASS/FAIL,
# and emits a machine- and auditor-readable evidence record on stdout.
#
# This is the EVALUATE step of the loop expressed as code. It is deliberately
# free of network, cloud, and scanner dependencies: it consumes a scan result
# that some scanner already produced. In the real pipeline the scanner runs
# first; here we prove the gate decision against committed fixtures.
#
# Usage:   gate.sh <checkov-result.json> <control-map.csv> [severity-floor]
# Default severity-floor: HIGH
# Exit:    0 = control set PASSES (build proceeds)
#          1 = control set FAILS  (build blocked)
#          2 = usage / input error
#
# Dependencies: bash + coreutils + awk only. No jq, no network.
set -euo pipefail

RESULT="${1:-}"
CONTROL_MAP="${2:-}"
FLOOR="${3:-HIGH}"

if [ -z "$RESULT" ] || [ -z "$CONTROL_MAP" ]; then
  echo "usage: gate.sh <checkov-result.json> <control-map.csv> [severity-floor]" >&2
  exit 2
fi
[ -f "$RESULT" ]      || { echo "ERROR: scan result not found: $RESULT" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -f "$CONTROL_MAP" ] || { echo "ERROR: control map not found: $CONTROL_MAP" >&2; exit 2; }

# Rank severities so the floor is a numeric comparison, not a string match.
sev_rank() {
  case "$1" in
    CRITICAL) echo 4 ;;
    HIGH)     echo 3 ;;
    MEDIUM)   echo 2 ;;
    LOW)      echo 1 ;;
    *)        echo 0 ;;
  esac
}
FLOOR_RANK="$(sev_rank "$FLOOR")"
[ "$FLOOR_RANK" -gt 0 ] || { echo "ERROR: unknown severity floor: $FLOOR" >&2; exit 2; }

# Extract failed checks from the JSON. We do NOT require jq: the relevant fields
# (check_id, check_name, severity) appear as quoted "key": "value" pairs, and
# every failed check is an object inside the "failed_checks" array. A single awk
# pass tracks bracket/brace depth so it isolates exactly the failed_checks array
# (correctly stepping over nested arrays like "file_line_range": [1, 4]), then
# emits one tab-separated record per object: check_id, severity, check_name.
#
# This is a pragmatic parser for THIS well-formed, machine-generated shape, not
# a general JSON parser. The real lab pipes real scanner output through jq; the
# fixture parser keeps the happy path dependency-free.
extract_failed() {
  awk '
    BEGIN { instr = 0; arm = 0; depth = 0; arraydepth = 0; objbuf = "" }
    {
      line = $0
      # If this line names the failed_checks key, arm so the next "[" opens
      # our array. The "[" can be on the same line, so arm before scanning.
      if (line ~ /"failed_checks"[ \t]*:/) arm = 1
      n = length(line)
      for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        c = substr(line, i, 1)
        prev = (i > 1) ? substr(line, i-1, 1) : ""
        # String-literal tracking so structural chars inside strings dont count.
        if (c == "\"" && prev != "\\") { instr = !instr }

        # Buffer EVERY char while we are inside a top-level object of the array,
        # including string content (we need the field values).
        if (collecting) objbuf = objbuf c

        if (instr) continue   # only structure decisions below ignore strings

        if (c == "[") {
          depth++
          if (arm == 1) { arraydepth = depth; arm = 0 }
        } else if (c == "]") {
          if (arraydepth && depth == arraydepth) arraydepth = 0
          depth--
        } else if (c == "{") {
          if (arraydepth && depth == arraydepth && !collecting) {
            collecting = 1; objbuf = "{"; objlevel = 0
          }
          if (collecting) objlevel++
        } else if (c == "}") {
          if (collecting) {
            objlevel--
            if (objlevel == 0) {
              cid = field(objbuf, "check_id")
              sev = field(objbuf, "severity")
              nm  = field(objbuf, "check_name")
              if (cid != "") {
                if (sev == "") sev = "UNKNOWN"
                if (nm  == "") nm  = "unknown"
                printf "%s\t%s\t%s\n", cid, sev, nm
              }
              collecting = 0; objbuf = ""
            }
          }
        }
      }
      if (collecting) objbuf = objbuf "\n"
    }
    function field(s, key,   re, m) {
      re = "\"" key "\"[ \t]*:[ \t]*\"[^\"]*\""
      if (match(s, re)) {
        m = substr(s, RSTART, RLENGTH)
        sub(/^.*:[ \t]*"/, "", m)
        sub(/"$/, "", m)
        return m
      }
      return ""
    }
  ' "$RESULT"
}

# Look a check_id up in the control map; print "control_id|control_title" or "UNMAPPED".
map_control() {
  awk -F, -v want="$1" '
    NR == 1 { next }                      # skip header
    $1 == want { print $2 "|" $3; found=1; exit }
    END { if (!found) print "UNMAPPED|unmapped check (no control owner)" }
  ' "$CONTROL_MAP"
}

echo "=== GRC IaC Gate — evidence record ==="
echo "scan_result: $RESULT"
echo "control_map: $CONTROL_MAP"
echo "severity_floor: $FLOOR"
echo "evaluated_at: ${GATE_FAKE_TIME:-$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)}"
echo "---"

BLOCKING=0
EVALUATED=0
while IFS=$'\t' read -r cid sev name; do
  [ -n "${cid:-}" ] || continue
  EVALUATED=$((EVALUATED + 1))
  rank="$(sev_rank "$sev")"
  mapping="$(map_control "$cid")"
  control_id="${mapping%%|*}"
  control_title="${mapping#*|}"
  if [ "$rank" -ge "$FLOOR_RANK" ]; then
    verdict="BLOCK"
    BLOCKING=$((BLOCKING + 1))
  else
    verdict="below-floor (not blocking)"
  fi
  echo "FAILED  $cid  [$sev]  -> $control_id ($control_title)  : $verdict"
  echo "        $name"
done < <(extract_failed)

echo "---"
echo "failed_checks_evaluated: $EVALUATED"
echo "blocking_at_or_above_${FLOOR}: $BLOCKING"

if [ "$BLOCKING" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "GATE_DECISION: FAIL  (build blocked — $BLOCKING control(s) violated at/above $FLOOR)"
  exit 1
fi

echo "GATE_DECISION: PASS  (no violations at/above $FLOOR — build proceeds, evidence emitted)"
exit 0

m13.library:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Module 13 control-check library. Offline by construction: no network, no cloud SDK, no jq.
# JSON parsing uses `bun` when it is on PATH (a real parser, robust to any formatting) and falls
# back to pure bash + coreutils + awk on a bare machine — same output contract either way.
#
# CONTROL: CC6.1-s3-public-access-block
#   Claim: "every S3 bucket has all four public-access-block settings enabled."
#
# The check reads a captured state snapshot (JSON) and returns a verdict a machine can act on:
#   stdout    = a single PASS/FAIL line, then one "NONCOMPLIANT <name>" line per drifted bucket
#   exit code = 0 when the control PASSES, 1 when it FAILS (drift), 2 when it could evaluate ZERO
#               resources and therefore FAILS CLOSED (refuses to report a green verdict it cannot
#               justify). That exit code is the hinge that turns a check into automation — no human
#               has to read the output, and a non-zero is never silently treated as healthy.
#
# Design note: this library never calls `set -e`. It is sourced by callers that may or may not
# run under errexit, so it preserves the caller's shell options and signals only through return
# codes. (An earlier version forced `set -e` and leaked it into the caller — fixed.)

# normalize_buckets <state-json-file>
# Flattens a captured-state snapshot to ONE LINE PER BUCKET — the form the evaluator judges.
# Each emitted line is: "<name>\t<block_public_acls>\t<block_public_policy>\t<ignore_public_acls>\t<restrict_public_buckets>"
# with each flag rendered as the literal "true" or "false".
#
# This MUST work on PRETTY-PRINTED JSON. Real `aws ... --output json`, `jq .`, and AWS Config
# exports are multi-line — the bucket name and its flags land on DIFFERENT physical lines. An
# earlier version matched a bucket only when "name" AND "restrict_public_buckets" appeared on the
# SAME line, so every pretty-printed snapshot parsed to zero buckets and silently PASSED a public
# bucket. Fixed: we normalise first (parse the whole document), then evaluate the normalised rows.
#
# Two parsers, same output contract, both OFFLINE (no network, no cloud SDK):
#   1) bun, if present — a real JSON parser, robust to any whitespace, key order, or nesting.
#   2) a pure-awk fallback for a bare machine — walks the "buckets" array brace-by-brace, so a
#      bucket object spread across many lines is collapsed into one normalised row.
normalize_buckets() {
  local state="$1"
  if command -v bun >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    bun -e '
      const fs = require("fs");
      const doc = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8"));
      const buckets = Array.isArray(doc.buckets) ? doc.buckets : [];
      const flag = (b, k) => (b[k] === true ? "true" : "false");
      for (const b of buckets) {
        const name = typeof b.name === "string" ? b.name : "";
        process.stdout.write([name,
          flag(b, "block_public_acls"), flag(b, "block_public_policy"),
          flag(b, "ignore_public_acls"), flag(b, "restrict_public_buckets")].join("\t") + "\n");
      }
    ' "$state"
    return 0
  fi
  # Pure-awk fallback for a bare machine (bash + coreutils + awk, no bun). Read the WHOLE document
  # as one record (RS=""), then walk only the "buckets" array brace-by-brace, collapsing each
  # {...} object — however it is wrapped across lines — into one normalised row. A bucket is
  # recognised by its "name" key, NEVER by the accident of which keys share a physical line.
  awk 'BEGIN { RS = "\0" }
    # val(buf,key): the literal value of "key" in object text buf — "true"/"false" for booleans,
    # the unquoted string for string values, or "" when the key is absent.
    function val(buf, key,   re, m) {
      re = "\"" key "\"[ \t\r\n]*:[ \t\r\n]*"
      if (match(buf, re "true"))  return "true"
      if (match(buf, re "false")) return "false"
      if (match(buf, "\"" key "\"[ \t\r\n]*:[ \t\r\n]*\"")) {
        m = substr(buf, RSTART + RLENGTH); sub(/".*$/, "", m); return m
      }
      return ""
    }
    function emit(buf,   nm) {
      nm = val(buf, "name")
      if (nm == "") return            # not a bucket object (no name) — skip
      printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", nm,
        (val(buf,"block_public_acls")=="true"?"true":"false"),
        (val(buf,"block_public_policy")=="true"?"true":"false"),
        (val(buf,"ignore_public_acls")=="true"?"true":"false"),
        (val(buf,"restrict_public_buckets")=="true"?"true":"false")
    }
    {
      doc = $0
      # Locate the "buckets" array and scan only from there, so a stray bracket elsewhere in the
      # document cannot be mistaken for the bucket list.
      if (!match(doc, /"buckets"[ \t\r\n]*:[ \t\r\n]*\[/)) exit 0
      i = RSTART + RLENGTH        # first char inside the [ ... ] array
      depth = 0; obj = ""; inobj = 0
      n = length(doc)
      for (; i <= n; i++) {
        c = substr(doc, i, 1)
        if (depth == 0 && c == "]") break       # end of the buckets array
        if (c == "{") { depth++; if (depth == 1) { obj = ""; inobj = 1; continue } }
        if (c == "}") { depth--; if (depth == 0) { emit(obj); inobj = 0; continue } }
        if (inobj) obj = obj c
      }
    }
  ' "$state"
}

# evaluate_control <state-json-file>
# Emits a machine-readable verdict on stdout. Returns 0 (pass) / 1 (fail/drift) / 2 (no resources).
# Deterministic: the same snapshot always yields the same verdict.
#
# FAIL CLOSED: if the snapshot parses to ZERO buckets (empty list, wrong shape, unparseable),
# this does NOT emit a green verdict — it refuses to pass and returns non-zero. A monitor that
# silently passes when it evaluated nothing is worse than no monitor: it manufactures evidence
# of compliance from the absence of data.
evaluate_control() {
  local state="$1"
  # Normalise to one row per bucket FIRST, then judge the rows. A bucket is COMPLIANT only when
  # all four public-access-block flags are true; otherwise it is NONCOMPLIANT (drift).
  # rows: "<name>\t<acls>\t<policy>\t<ignore>\t<restrict>"
  local rows total noncompliant
  rows="$(normalize_buckets "$state")"
  total="$(printf '%s' "$rows" | grep -c . || true)"

  # Refuse to pass on an empty evaluation — fail closed.
  if [ "$total" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "ERROR control=CC6.1-s3-public-access-block evaluated=0 — refusing to pass: zero resources evaluated (empty, unparsed, or wrong-shape snapshot)" >&2
    echo "FAIL control=CC6.1-s3-public-access-block evaluated=0 noncompliant=0 reason=no-resources-evaluated"
    return 2
  fi

  # A row is NONCOMPLIANT unless every one of its four flags is exactly "true".
  noncompliant="$(printf '%s\n' "$rows" | awk -F'\t' '
    NF>=5 && !($2=="true" && $3=="true" && $4=="true" && $5=="true") { print $1 }
  ')"

  if [ -z "$noncompliant" ]; then
    echo "PASS control=CC6.1-s3-public-access-block evaluated=${total} noncompliant=0"
    return 0
  fi
  echo "FAIL control=CC6.1-s3-public-access-block evaluated=${total} noncompliant=$(printf '%s\n' "$noncompliant" | grep -c .)"
  printf 'NONCOMPLIANT %s\n' $noncompliant
  return 1
}

# emit_evidence <state-json-file> <evidence-dir>
# Runs the check, writes a timestamped immutable evidence record, appends one row to the
# append-only ledger (the 30-day-history substrate a dashboard tile reads), and — only on drift —
# writes an alert file. Returns the check's exit code so the caller can branch on PASS/FAIL.
emit_evidence() {
  local state="$1" evdir="$2"
  mkdir -p "$evdir"
  local captured run_id verdict_line rc full record
  captured="$(awk -F'"' '/"captured_at"/{print $4; exit}' "$state")"
  # Fall back to a wall-clock stamp when the snapshot carries no captured_at (e.g. a malformed or
  # empty state) so the fail-closed record + alert still get a stable, unique filename.
  [ -n "$captured" ] || captured="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
  run_id="run-$(printf '%s' "$captured" | tr -cd '0-9')"
  record="$evdir/${run_id}.evidence"

  # Capture the verdict WITHOUT toggling shell options. `if cmd; then …` neutralises errexit for
  # this one call, so a FAIL (return 1) does not abort an errexit-enabled caller mid-function.
  if full="$(evaluate_control "$state")"; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
  verdict_line="$(printf '%s\n' "$full" | head -1)"

  # Immutable per-run evidence record — generated by the same code that did the evaluating,
  # so it cannot drift from what was actually checked.
  {
    echo "control_id=CC6.1-s3-public-access-block"
    echo "captured_at=${captured}"
    echo "verdict=${verdict_line}"
    echo "exit_code=${rc}"
    echo "source_state=$(basename "$state")"
  } > "$record"

  # Append-only ledger: one row per run. This is the history a dashboard tile reads to draw
  # "current state + 30-day trend". Append-only because evidence you can rewrite is not evidence.
  echo "${captured} ${run_id} rc=${rc} ${verdict_line}" >> "$evdir/ledger.log"

  # Alert fires ONLY on drift (non-zero exit). A PASS leaves no alert behind — silence is the
  # signal that the control is holding. A fail-closed "no resources evaluated" (rc=2) is also a
  # drift the responder must see: the monitor could not confirm the control, so it must not be
  # mistaken for healthy silence.
  if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
    {
      echo "ALERT control=CC6.1-s3-public-access-block captured_at=${captured}"
      echo "${verdict_line}"
      if [ "$rc" -eq 2 ]; then
        echo "drifted_resource=<none — evaluated 0 resources; snapshot empty, unparsed, or wrong shape>"
      else
        printf '%s\n' "$full" | awk '/^NONCOMPLIANT /{print "drifted_resource=" $2}'
      fi
    } > "$evdir/alert-${run_id}.txt"
  fi
  return "$rc"
}

seed.validate-capstone.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Capstone coverage validator. Asserts the manifest covers all 7 loop stages
# (each mapped to an existing artifact) and the before/after writeup is present.
# Pure bash + coreutils + awk. Exits 0 on full coverage, non-zero otherwise.
set -euo pipefail
MANIFEST="${1:?usage: validate-capstone.sh <capstone-manifest.yaml>}"
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$MANIFEST")" && pwd)"
test -f "$MANIFEST" || { echo "FAIL: manifest not found: $MANIFEST"; exit 2; }

STAGES="UNDERSTAND LOCATE QUERY EVALUATE EVIDENCE MONITOR OWN"
fail=0

# Pull "key: value" pairs from the indented loop_coverage block only.
coverage_value() {
  awk -v key="$1" '
    /^loop_coverage:/ { inblk=1; next }
    inblk && /^[^[:space:]]/ { inblk=0 }
    inblk {
      line=$0
      sub(/^[[:space:]]+/, "", line)
      n=index(line, ":")
      if (n>0) {
        k=substr(line,1,n-1)
        v=substr(line,n+1)
        sub(/^[[:space:]]+/, "", v); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", v)
        if (k==key) { print v; exit }
      }
    }
  ' "$MANIFEST"
}

echo "checking loop coverage..."
for stage in $STAGES; do
  artifact="$(coverage_value "$stage")"
  if [ -z "$artifact" ]; then
    printf "  %-11s MISSING (no artifact mapped)\n" "$stage"
    fail=1
    continue
  fi
  if [ -e "$ROOT/$artifact" ]; then
    printf "  %-11s ok  -> %s\n" "$stage" "$artifact"
  else
    printf "  %-11s MISSING (artifact not found: %s)\n" "$stage" "$artifact"
    fail=1
  fi
done

echo "checking before/after..."
ba="$(awk -F: '/^before_after:/ { v=$2; sub(/^[[:space:]]+/,"",v); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/,"",v); print v; exit }' "$MANIFEST")"
if [ -n "$ba" ] && [ -e "$ROOT/$ba" ]; then
  echo "  before/after ok -> $ba"
else
  echo "  before/after MISSING (no before_after pointer or file not found)"
  fail=1
fi

if [ "$fail" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: capstone coverage incomplete — close the named gaps before shipping"
  exit 1
fi
echo "PASS: all 7 loop stages covered; before/after present"
